name: Chamath Palihapitiya
milestone_by_age_26: Became AOL's youngest VP and led the instant messaging division around 2004 at age ~27–28 (born Sept 1976); Business Insider's 'age 26' claim conflicts with DOB math. Joined Facebook in 2007 at age 30–31. No clearly dated material milestone at age ≤26 verified.
early_history_summary: Born in Galle, Sri Lanka (1976), emigrated to Canada as a child; raised in a financially precarious household. Graduated University of Waterloo electrical engineering (1999), worked as a derivatives trader, then joined Winamp/AOL (2001) before Facebook (2007) and founding Social Capital (2011).
evidence_summary: Primary fame and wealth came from Facebook growth leadership (2007–2011) and later Social Capital / SPAC / All-In activity, all after age 26. AOL VP is the closest early claim, but sources place it in 2004 when he was 27–28.

name: Chris Putnam
milestone_by_age_26: No reliable birth year found. Known for 2005 Facebook profile prank/hack that led to a Facebook engineering job in 2006; without a confirmed birth year, a material milestone by age 26 cannot be verified. (CSV name 'Chris Putman' matches public accounts of Chris Putnam.)
early_history_summary: Around late 2005, Chris Putnam (with collaborators) built Facebook pranks that went viral; Facebook hired him rather than prosecuting. He later worked on Facebook video and other engineering roles. College at Georgia Southern is mentioned in first-person accounts.
evidence_summary: The Facebook hire is a notable story but eligibility requires a dated age ≤26 milestone; no birth year appears in Wikipedia or other reviewed sources for this batch candidate.

name: Alexandra Boltasseva
milestone_by_age_26: Completed a Ph.D. in electrical engineering at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) in 2004 at age 26, with dissertation work on integrated-optics components using long-range surface plasmon polaritons, and received a Danish Technical Research Council Talent Project grant the same year.
early_history_summary: Born in Kanash, Chuvashia (1978). Earned B.S. (1999) and M.S. (2000, highest honors) in applied physics and mathematics at Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology with research at Lebedev Physical Institute. Moved to DTU for a nanophotonics Ph.D. under Sergey I. Bozhevolnyi, finishing in 2004 at age 26, then worked in Danish photonics startups and returned to academia.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace in Chuvashia; later married fellow nanophotonics researcher Vladimir Shalaev.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIPT elite physics pipeline, DTU nanophotonics PhD, early lab access, mentor Bozhevolnyi
evidence_summary: Boltasseva followed a high-selectivity physics/engineering path from MIPT through DTU, completing a specialized plasmonics Ph.D. by 26. Early awards (high-school physics olympiads, Lenin scholarship, Talent Project grant) indicate sustained scarce technical depth rather than inherited capital or audience. Later TR35 (2011), OSA/IEEE fellowships, and Purdue named professorship build on that early research foundation.
starting_point: Born 1978 in Kanash, Chuvashia (then USSR); early academic path through Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology; family class details not documented.
current_position: Ron and Dotty Garvin Tonjes Distinguished Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Purdue University; leading nanophotonics/plasmonics researcher and Optica fellow.

trajectory.event: Completed M.S. in applied physics and mathematics with highest honors at MIPT after research at Lebedev Physical Institute.
Earned Ph.D. in electrical engineering at DTU on long-range surface plasmon polariton integrated-optics components; received Danish Talent Project grant.
Joined Purdue University as assistant professor after academic and startup roles in Denmark; later rose to distinguished professor.
Named to MIT Technology Review TR35 young innovators list for nanophotonics work.
Elected Fellow of The Optical Society (Optica) for contributions to nanophotonics and plasmonic materials.
Received Optica R.W. Wood Prize and was elected APS Fellow for broad impact in nanophotonics and metamaterials.

name: David Heinemeier Hansson
category: Software engineer / open-source framework creator (Ruby on Rails)
milestone_by_age_26: Extracted and open-sourced Ruby on Rails from Basecamp work at 37signals in July 2004 at age 24; the framework became a defining web-development platform used by companies such as GitHub, Shopify, and Airbnb.
early_history_summary: Born in Copenhagen (1979). Learned PHP in high school building gaming review sites and ran the Danish gaming community Daily Rush (1999–2001). Hired by Jason Fried after offering PHP help, he built Basecamp and created Rails as the underlying framework, releasing it open source in 2004 before moving to Chicago in 2005.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond Danish upbringing in Copenhagen.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early web/PHP reps, Jason Fried partnership, Basecamp product immersion, open-source distribution
evidence_summary: DHH built real web products as a teen and early-20s freelancer before formal Rails fame. The decisive advantage was extracting a reusable framework from shipping Basecamp with Jason Fried, then releasing it open source into a rising Ruby/web-app wave. Family capital and elite institutions are not documented as drivers; the partnership and product immersion are.
starting_point: Born 1979 in Copenhagen, Denmark; early self-taught programmer via gaming sites; family socioeconomic details not documented.
current_position: Creator of Ruby on Rails; co-owner and CTO of 37signals (Basecamp, HEY); author and endurance racing driver.

trajectory.event: Founded Daily Rush, a Danish online gaming news site and community, while building web skills in PHP.
Open-sourced Ruby on Rails after extracting the framework from Basecamp development at 37signals.
Named Google/O'Reilly Hacker of the Year for Rails; moved from Denmark to Chicago and became 37signals partner/CTO path.
Rails and Basecamp were widely adopted; co-authored influential 37signals product books beginning around this era.
Co-authored bestseller Rework with Jason Fried, extending product philosophy influence beyond the Rails community.
Won the GTE Am class at the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Aston Martin Racing.
Continued leading 37signals product strategy including HEY email and the company's independent SaaS stance.

name: Joy Buolamwini
category: Computer scientist / AI bias researcher and founder
milestone_by_age_26: Named a 2013 Rhodes Scholar in November 2012 at age 22 after graduating Georgia Tech in computer science; by age 26 (2016) she had also founded the Algorithmic Justice League while at MIT Media Lab.
early_history_summary: Born in Edmonton (1990) to Ghanaian immigrant parents; raised partly in the U.S. South. Taught herself web programming as a child, competed as a student-athlete, and graduated Georgia Tech (2012) as a Stamps President's Scholar. Won Fulbright (Zambia, 2013) and Rhodes (Oxford) pathways before MIT Media Lab work that produced Gender Shades and AJL.
family_context_summary: Born in Canada to Ghanaian immigrants; has described father as an academic and mother as an artist. Specific family financial platform not documented in detail.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father academic, mother artist per her public self-description; not a tech-industry apprenticeship pipeline.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Georgia Tech, Rhodes, Fulbright, MIT Media Lab, early coding, outsider lens on facial recognition
evidence_summary: Buolamwini stacked elite scholarships (Stamps, Anita Borg, Astronaut, Fulbright, Rhodes) into MIT Media Lab research that exposed commercial facial-analysis bias. Early coding from childhood and competitive athletics show high agency; family was immigrant academic/arts rather than tech capital. Founding AJL at 26 and Gender Shades (with Timnit Gebru) converted institutional access into field-defining impact.
starting_point: Born 1990 in Edmonton, Alberta, to Ghanaian immigrants; grew up between Ghana, Mississippi/Tennessee, and other places; father academic, mother artist.
current_position: Founder of the Algorithmic Justice League; AI researcher, author of Unmasking AI (2023), and leading public voice on algorithmic bias and AI accountability.

trajectory.event: Graduated Georgia Tech in computer science and was named a 2013 Rhodes Scholar.
Completed Fulbright work in Zambia supporting youth technology creators and began Oxford Rhodes studies.
Founded the Algorithmic Justice League and premiered The Coded Gaze mini-documentary on bias in facial analysis systems.
Published Gender Shades with Timnit Gebru, documenting large intersectional error disparities in commercial gender classification.
Testified before U.S. Congress on facial recognition risks; named to Fortune World's 50 Greatest Leaders and Time 100 Next.
Featured in the documentary Coded Bias, which brought her research and AJL work to a global audience.
Published Unmasking AI and appeared on TIME100 AI; advised on U.S. AI policy discussions.

name: Nathan Adams
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded the Bukkit Minecraft server modding platform (work began Dec 2010 at age 19) and was hired by Mojang on February 28, 2012 at age 20 as a Minecraft developer focused on the mod API.
early_history_summary: Born July 23, 1991, in Shrewsbury, UK. Learned programming via MSN bots around age 10. After secondary school and college rejection, worked at a small web shop, co-started Bukkit with other hMod developers, worked at Curse, then joined Mojang full-time in 2012—becoming a long-time public face of Minecraft Java development as Dinnerbone.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond UK origin in Shrewsbury.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bukkit OSS team, Minecraft wave, Curse to Mojang path, early programming, college rejection constraint
evidence_summary: Adams's breakout came from deep Minecraft server-modding work with peers (Bukkit), not elite schools or family capital. College rejection and early web jobs preceded open-source visibility that Mojang converted into an official role at age 20. The Minecraft cultural wave and high-trust Bukkit team were decisive multipliers.
starting_point: Born 1991 in Shrewsbury, United Kingdom; self-taught programmer from childhood; family background otherwise not documented.
current_position: Long-time Mojang Studios engineer known as Dinnerbone; technical leadership contributions across Minecraft Java/Bedrock and launcher work over more than a decade.

trajectory.event: With peers, began Bukkit as an open-source Minecraft server modding API/platform after hMod stagnation.
Hired by Mojang (Feb 28, 2012) to work on Minecraft's mod API; first office day March 27, 2012.
Public Bukkit ownership controversy after EvilSeph's shutdown notice; Adams confirmed Mojang ownership and continued support work.
Temporarily left the Minecraft team for other Mojang work before later rejoining.
Confirmed return to the Minecraft development team.
Publicly noted a multi-year health-related leave from work while remaining associated with Mojang/Minecraft.
Announced return to Minecraft development activity.

name: Francine Berman
milestone_by_age_26: Born 1951; B.A. UCLA 1973 (age ~22) and M.S. 1976 (age ~25) were ordinary academic progress, while Ph.D. completed in 1979 at age 28. Major leadership milestones (SDSC director 2001, Ken Kennedy Award 2009) arrived decades after age 26. No material career breakthrough by 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born Glendale, California. Mathematics degrees at UCLA and University of Washington (Ph.D. 1979). Academic career at Purdue then UCSD; directed San Diego Supercomputer Center (2001–2009); later RPI VP for research and public-interest technology work at UMass Amherst.
evidence_summary: A highly accomplished senior computing leader, but fame and institutional leadership came mid-career, not by 26. Academic degrees alone do not meet the material ≤26 milestone bar here.

evidence_summary: React is tier-defining software, but eligibility requires verified age ≤26 at a material milestone. Birth year is not established by Wikipedia-level sources, so eligibility fails the verification bar.
